extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants, patent attorneys/agents, and patent examiners (Korea)
extracted.subtask_description: Examination guidance on claiming disclosure exceptions (Article 30 of the Korean Patent Act) and initial principles for assessing inventive step (Article 29), including procedural, evidential, and substantive examination criteria for domestic and international filings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure exception eligibility (Article 30)
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a person entitled to obtain a patent files an application within twelve months (six months for filings before March 15, 2012) of an action described in Article 30, the invention is considered not to fall under the public-disclosure bars of Article 29(1) when Article 29(1) or (2) otherwise applies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Two main sub-cases: (1) disclosure by a person with the right to obtain a patent; (2) disclosure against the intention of the person with the right. The general purpose is to allow an applicant to file despite prior disclosure if conditions are met (encourage early disclosure). Excludes cases where the application was laid open or registration published in Korea or a foreign country under treaty/law.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing requirement to claim disclosure exception
rubrics_metrics.description: An application relying on Article 30 must be filed within twelve months (six months if filing date earlier than March 15, 2012) of the date on which the invention was disclosed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Filing within the grace period is a strict formal requirement; for some filings (after July 29, 2015), supporting proof may be submitted within extended time windows (see procedural exceptions). The filing-time comparison is to the actual filing time (including hour/minute) for determining prior art.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statement of intent and supporting documents (formal procedural requirement)
rubrics_metrics.description: A person who intends to take advantage of Article 30(1)(1) must submit a written statement of that intention when filing and must submit documents proving the relevant facts within thirty days of the filing date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proving document may be submitted simultaneously with filing. For certain filings on/after July 29, 2015, the proving document can be submitted within 3 months from receipt of a certified copy of grant or within the period for amending specification/claims (but before registration publication). For international applications, the intention must be stated in the application and proof submitted within thirty days after the domestic reference date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure against intention (Article 30 subparagraph (2)) – requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: When an invention is disclosed against the intention of the entitled person, the entitled person must file within the twelve-month grace period (six months for earlier filings) but does not need to state the purport of Article 30 in the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The applicant must prove that the disclosure was against their intention; the examiner judges such claims case-by-case and accepts various forms of evidence where voluntary disclosure cannot be shown.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evidential matters required for examination of disclosure exception claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Matters required for examination are: (i) disclosure date, (ii) discloser, (iii) disclosure type, and (iv) content of the disclosed invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sufficiency is judged by whether these matters can be confirmed from submitted documents. If not specified (e.g., exhibition disclosure), supplementary documents (programs, catalogs, photos) and explanations may be requested. Examiner may order amendment or invalidate the claiming proceeding if deficiencies are not remedied.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formalities examination triggers and correction grounds
rubrics_metrics.description: On receipt of an application indicating intent to claim a disclosure exception, the examiner checks whether filing was within the 12/6 month period and whether the disclosure was by a person entitled to obtain a patent; the office issues correction notices if any of specified sub-grounds are present.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Four example grounds prompting correction notice: (1) discloser different from filer/inventor; (2) application filed after the grace period; (3) wrong disclosure date/type or incorrect info on proof documents; (4) submitted documents insufficient to prove relevant facts. Failure to amend in the designated period leads to invalidation of the Article 30 claim (filing still effective).

rubrics_metrics.name: Substantive examination outcome for valid Article 30 claims
rubrics_metrics.description: If no defects are found in application and supporting documents, disclosures falling under Article 30 are recognized as non-prior art for examination when Article 29(1) or (2) would otherwise apply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the claiming proceeding fails due to deficiencies, the submitted documents may instead be used as prior art against the application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multiple disclosures and inseparable disclosures rule
rubrics_metrics.description: If the entitled person disclosed the invention several times before filing, in principle Article 30 proceedings are taken for each disclosure; however, the indication of intention need not specify each disclosure if a general intention is recognized and evidential documents for disclosures are submitted within 30 days.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inseparably related disclosures (examples include multi-day tests, test + distributed explanations, editions of publications, exhibition display + catalog, oral presentation + booklet, lecture tours) may be treated together; subsequent disclosures inseparably related to the initial, properly claimed disclosure can enjoy the exception without separate proof.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exhibition disclosure evidential expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: Where disclosure occurred at an exhibition and the evidential document cannot specify the disclosed invention, supplementary documents specifying the invention (e.g., exhibition program, catalog, pamphlet, photos of display) and explanations can be requested.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If questions arise about fact relations (host, date, venue, exhibitor), additional documents proving those facts can be required. Examiner assesses whether the evidence sufficiently specifies content and fact relations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Third-party disclosure after initial non-considered disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: If a third person discloses the same invention between the initial disclosure (claimed under Article 30) and the filing date, the examiner shall reject the application for lack of novelty unless it is obvious the third-party disclosure was made by learning from the initial disclosure and applicant can prove otherwise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After issuing notice of grounds for rejection, the examiner will reject if the applicant cannot establish that (i) the third person disclosed after learning from the non-considered disclosure or (ii) the invention was filed against the applicant's intention. The burden is on applicant to rebut or prove sequence/causation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Same-day filings and related applications (Article 36 interaction)
rubrics_metrics.description: Where applicant A files claiming Article 30 within the grace period and a third person files application B for the same invention on the same filing date, Article 36(2) applies: A and B are related and applicants must consult to decide who obtains the patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner instructs both applicants to report consultation results (Article 36(6)) rather than issuing a rejection for novelty. If applicant B withdraws following consultation, applicant A may obtain a patent. B may be deemed to lack novelty because filed after disclosure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication or laid-open publication prevents Article 30 application
rubrics_metrics.description: If the application has been laid open or registered and published in Korea (patent gazette), Article 30 does not apply to the invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Normal filing leads to KIPO laying open under Article 64(1); such laying open is not voluntary and removes eligibility for Article 30. If KIPO mistakenly lays open before completion and the disclosure is against the applicant's intention, Article 30 may still be invoked.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosures covered by grace period (who/what qualifies)
rubrics_metrics.description: Disclosures that can be graced under Article 30(1)(1) include: disclosure by a person entitled to the patent, disclosure by a third party at that person's request, and disclosure by a third party referencing the invention with permission (including implied permission).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: entrusting a third party to disclose (with inventor/right holder named), press releases or scripts sent to newspaper, catalogs printed by employer. Even where name not stated, fact that the right holder authored/disclosed must be provable. References by others that cite inventor/company or catalogs count if permission exists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Joint inventors / joint presenters evidentiary rule
rubrics_metrics.description: When two or more persons jointly make an invention or file, if among presenters who disclosed the invention at least one presenter is the inventor or applicant, Article 30 may apply without further proof; if no relation exists, the applicant must submit documents proving entitlement, that disclosure was requested by right holder, or that permission to reference was obtained.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Required documents: (i) proof presenter is entitled to obtain patent, (ii) proof disclosure was at request of right holder, (iii) proof of permission for referencing the invention.

rubrics_metrics.name: International (PCT) application procedure for claiming disclosure exception
rubrics_metrics.description: For an international application, an applicant must state intention and submit proof within thirty days after the domestic reference date (Article 201(4)); declaration in PCT request form Box VIII(v) is treated as an application cover sheet declaration under Article 42(1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If declaration is included in PCT request form and supporting evidence is legitimately submitted within 30 days from the reference date, the PCT filing meets Article 30(2) requirements and KIPO will examine it as a regular claim to exceptions to lack of novelty (see PCT Rule 4.17). For national phase entries, submit within specified national-phase periods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedural relaxations for applications filed on/after July 29, 2015
rubrics_metrics.description: For applications filed on/after July 29, 2015, proving documents for Article 30 may be submitted within 3 months from the date of receiving a certified copy of grant or within the period to amend specification, drawings, or claims (provided before registration publication). Examiner will issue all grounds for rejection at once.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because applicant can invoke grace period within 3 months after grant or during amendment period, the examiner should issue all grounds for rejection together. If applicant remedies a rejection by claiming disclosure exception but new grounds arise from other documents, the examiner shall issue a first office action addressing the new grounds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Substantive exam – use of submitted proof if claim fails
rubrics_metrics.description: An examiner reviews all submitted documents; disclosures recognized under Article 30 are treated as non-prior art if the claim is valid. However, if the claim to exception fails because of deficiencies, the submitted documents may be used as prior art.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner must therefore ensure formal and substantive sufficiency of the Article 30 claim before excluding the disclosed material from prior-art consideration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'prior to filing' (time point precision)
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Prior to filing of a patent application' refers to the definite time (hours and minutes) of filing; foreign public disclosure that precedes the Korean filing time is prior art under Article 29(1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When checking worldwide disclosures, compare the exact time of foreign public disclosure to the Korean filing time (including hour/minute) to assess prior art status.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'person skilled in the art' for inventive step
rubrics_metrics.description: A hypothetical person having common general knowledge in the relevant art, the ability to use ordinary technical means for R&D (experiments, analysis, manufacture), exercise ordinary creativity in selecting materials/changing designs, and comprehend the state of the art in the field at the time of filing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes capacity to perform ordinary experiments and to understand common general knowledge; used as the benchmark for assessing whether an invention could have been easily made.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of inventions 'that could have been easily made' (inventive step threshold)
rubrics_metrics.description: An invention 'could have been easily made' where a person skilled in the art could have easily conceived the claimed invention by exercising ordinary creativity or motivation induced from prior art disclosures existing prior to filing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the claimed invention could have been easily made from prior art references, alone or in combination, it lacks inventive step under Article 29(2).

rubrics_metrics.name: General principles for determining inventive step
rubrics_metrics.description: Determine whether the invention as described in the claims could have been easily made by a person skilled in the art based on prior art references of Article 29(1); if so, the claim lacks inventive step. Assessment is done claim-by-claim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner may combine prior art references; determination of inventive step is separate from novelty but the office may notify grounds for rejection on both novelty and inventive step together when appropriate. Each claim must be assessed individually.
